# Upgrade rollback playbook — facts

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Before upgrading, record the current deployment and configuration, define explicit rollback triggers including performance problems and errors, and document the restore procedure, communication path, post-rollback monitoring, and failure review; validate the recovery process in staging. (medium confidence) — https://learn.percona.com/hubfs/eBooks/Percona_Mongo-Upgrade_Best_Practices.pdf · keywords: Upgrade rollback playbook · also: https://www.osseva.io/blog/mongodb-7-to-8-upgrade

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] For self-managed Community deployments, plan a 7.0-to-8.0 rollback as restoring a backup taken before the upgrade rather than relying on a binary downgrade; rehearse and time the restore before production. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/release-notes/8.0-downgrade/ · keywords: Upgrade rollback playbook · also: https://www.osseva.io/blog/mongodb-7-to-8-upgrade, https://learn.percona.com/hubfs/eBooks/Percona_Mongo-Upgrade_Best_Practices.pdf
- [statement] Set read-path rollback triggers against representative workload baselines instead of assuming every 8.0 read workload improves: MongoDB says performance gains vary by workload and configuration, and Percona's comparison of Percona Server for MongoDB 8.0.4 with 7.0.15 found individual tests where 7.0 was more than 5% faster. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-02-04) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/release-notes/8.0-upgrade-standalone/ · keywords: Upgrade rollback playbook · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-8-0-performance-does-it-live-up-to-the-hype/, https://www.percona.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Untitled-drawing-3.png

## Facts and statements

- [statement] As verified on 2026-10-23, MongoDB's 8.0 documentation says binary downgrades are unsupported for Community Edition, Enterprise binary downgrade requires support assistance, and only single-version downgrades are supported. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/release-notes/8.0-downgrade/ · keywords: Upgrade rollback playbook · also: https://www.osseva.io/blog/mongodb-7-to-8-upgrade
- [statement] After installing MongoDB 8.0 binaries on a 7.0 deployment, keep FCV at 7.0 through a burn-in and raise it to 8.0 only after tests make downgrade unlikely; FCV 8.0 enables persisted features that are incompatible with 7.0 and can complicate downgrade. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/8.0-upgrade-replica-set/ · keywords: Upgrade rollback playbook · also: https://www.osseva.io/blog/mongodb-7-to-8-upgrade
- [statement] Atlas Core has a separate rollback path: an in-place major-version downgrade requires FCV to have been pinned before the upgrade; without that pin, MongoDB documents point-in-time or snapshot restore to a new cluster running the previous major version. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/major-version-downgrade/ · keywords: Upgrade rollback playbook
